ooRexx HTTPS Server v0.4.4 liveness diagnosis

Independent target-host evidence eliminated several earlier hypotheses:
- v0.3: unrestricted concurrent TLS/native activity could segfault under reset pressure.
- v0.4: one global serialized native gate removed the crash but reset stress timed out.
- v0.4.1: four serialized native lanes still timed out on the target host.
- v0.4.2: OpenSSL socket BIOs were removed completely and RxSock became sole network-I/O owner, yet the same mixed reset storm still timed out in wave 1.

The remaining common scaling behavior was admission: every accepted TCP peer immediately received a fresh ooRexx activity before TLS was established. Reset/abort peers therefore competed with valid clients for interpreter scheduling and lifecycle cleanup merely by completing TCP accept(). Ordinary 16-way HTTPS passed on the target while the 32-peer mixed wave failed, matching that boundary.

v0.4.4 response:
- fixed connection worker set: 16 by default;
- bounded FIFO of accepted sockets: 64 by default;
- accept() only acquires/pins the connection lease and enqueues it;
- workers process queued connections synchronously; there is no conn~start('run') per peer;
- failed/incomplete TLS handshakes do not perform SSL_shutdown/close_notify;
- direct peer EOF during handshake is normal ABORT/noise, not ERROR-log amplification;
- OpenSSL remains one serialized in-memory native lane;
- RxSock remains sole descriptor/network-I/O owner.

Local evidence is deliberately not treated as closure for the independent OpenSSL 3.5.3 host. The decisive closure test is the unchanged 16-good + 16-reset wave there.
